Averaging within-user fractional ranks across 5 independently-seeded FM models will improve validation primary by ~0.0016 over a single-seed model, because rank averaging reduces variance in the ordering decisions that directly determine GAUC and nDCG@5
mechanism: Each FM seed produces slightly different score values due to random initialization; some seeds rank a pair correctly, others incorrectly. Averaging fractional ranks (not raw scores) aggregates the ordering signal in rank space, which is exactly what GAUC and nDCG@5 measure. Rank-space averaging works better than score-space averaging because the metric is ordinal: a seed that is confidently wrong in score space but correct in rank space still contributes correctly after rank conversion.

evidence.task_structure: With only ~5 impressions per user, each pairwise comparison is high-variance. A single model's random initialization can systematically mis-rank a pair; ensemble majority reduces this. The within-user structure means rank averaging is directly optimizing the evaluation criterion.

This was measured on the same split with the same FM model.

hypothesis: Replacing pointwise BCE with a BPR pairwise loss (sampling positive/negative pairs within each user per batch) will improve GAUC by directly optimizing the pairwise ranking objective, producing a gain of >0.002 over the current best
mechanism: GAUC is per-user AUC = fraction of (positive, negative) pairs where the positive scores higher. BPR loss minimizes -log(sigmoid(score_pos - score_neg)) for within-user pairs, which is the exact pairwise objective GAUC measures. Pointwise BCE does not see the relative ordering of items within a user's list, only absolute label prediction. With ~5 items/user and 1-2 positives, each user contributes ~3-6 pairs; BPR directly trains the model to get these pairs right.

evidence.task_structure: GAUC is a pairwise metric computed within users; with ~5 impressions/user the evaluation is almost entirely determined by pairwise ordering of 1-2 positives against 3-4 negatives within each user's tiny list
evidence.previous_experiments: Node 0-3 all use pointwise BCE; the ranking objective category has 4 accepted runs out of 25 with best delta +0.0015, but those attempts were on older configurations without the CTR features and rank averaging that our current best uses
evidence.literature: [W2512971201] YouTube DNN recommendation paper discusses that direct optimization of ranking metrics outperforms pointwise approaches for ranking tasks. The BPR mechanism is well-established for within-user pairwise ranking.

GBDT can capture non-linear interactions between features natively without discretizing continuous inputs, and with the right feature set (user history statistics crossed with video attributes) it may handle the within-user ranking task better. Features: the 5 standard fields encoded + continuous features (duration_ms, video CTR, author CTR computed from training history). Expected gain: +0.003 to +0.010 over baseline if ranking objective + continuous features help.
